title: Ramayana Tour in Sri Lanka: Private-Car Trail, Itineraries & Prices
description: The Ramayana places in Sri Lanka — Ashok Vatika, Ramboda Hanuman, Munneswaram, Ravana Falls — with timings, steps, dress code and two private-car trips.

hero.eyebrow: Ceylon Hop guide · The Ramayana Trail
hero.sub: Ashok Vatika, Hanuman’s hill, the temples where Rama prayed. Thirteen places across the island that tradition ties to the epic, and how to visit them at a gentle pace in your own car.

lede: Six days covers the heart of the trail:
ledeEm: Chilaw’s temples, Ramboda’s Hanuman, then two nights in the hills around Ashok Vatika.
ledeTail: Eight days takes you south with the story, to Ella, Kataragama and Galle.
sitesSub: In the order we’d visit them, with timings, steps and our honest tip. These are places of tradition and belief, not proven history, and in Sri Lanka Ravana is also respected as a great king, so we tell both sides of the story.

sites.name: Seetha Amman Kovil · Ashok Vatika
sites.text: Tradition holds that this is Ashok Vatika, the garden where Ravana kept Sita and where Hanuman found her and gave her Rama’s ring. Today it is a living Hindu temple beside a stream at Seetha Eliya, on the road from Nuwara Eliya to Hakgala. The temple was re-consecrated in May 2024 with water brought from the Sarayu at Ayodhya.
spec: Seetha Eliya · 5–8 km from Nuwara Eliya
sites.tip: Come for the morning puja, before the coaches. The floor is cold at 1,800 m, so bring thick socks for after you take your shoes off. Skip the boulders by the stream with older parents.

sites.name: Shri Bhakta Hanuman Temple, Ramboda
sites.text: Tradition holds that Hanuman passed through these hills searching for Sita. The Chinmaya Mission temple (2002) has an 18-foot Hanuman looking out over the tea, and a vegetarian restaurant.
spec: On the A5, Kandy → Nuwara Eliya
sites.tip: Arrive before 1 pm and have lunch here. The temple restaurant is a good vegetarian lunch stop.

sites.name: Munneswaram & Manavari, Chilaw
sites.text: Tradition holds that Rama installed a lingam at Manavari and worshipped Shiva at Munneswaram after the war, to atone for killing Ravana. Both are active temples. Munneswaram’s month-long festival in August–September draws Hindu, Buddhist, Catholic and Muslim pilgrims.
spec: Chilaw · about 1–1½ h from the airport

sites.name: Divurumpola, near Welimada
sites.text: Tradition holds that Sita took her agni pariksha, the trial by fire, here. Today it is a Buddhist temple, with a Bo tree, stupas and statues of Rama, Sita and Hanuman. Offerings follow Buddhist custom.
spec: About 4 km off the Nuwara Eliya–Welimada road

sites.name: Ravana Falls, Ella
sites.text: Tradition holds that Sita was hidden in caves behind the falls. You see it from the roadside on the Ella–Wellawaya road, so it’s an easy stop for everyone.

more.name: Hakgala Botanical Garden
more.text: The other place claimed as Ashok Vatika, on the same road as Seetha Amman, so visiting both settles the question. Shady, easy paths; foreign adult entry LKR 3,540.

more.name: Gayathri Peedam
more.text: Where tradition places Indrajit’s ritual before battle. Active shrine 3 km from town, about 80 steps.

more.name: Kelaniya Temple
more.text: Where Vibhishana is said to have been crowned. A Buddhist temple with coronation murals, 10 km from the city. About 50 steps.

more.name: Panchamuga Anjaneyar
more.text: Five-faced Hanuman at Kalubowila. A devotional stop, not a legend site. Good for your last morning.

more.name: Kataragama
more.text: Where Skanda is said to have helped Rama. Hindu, Buddhist and Muslim pilgrims share the evening puja.

more.name: Ussangoda
more.text: Red earth said to be scorched by Hanuman’s burning tail. A national park on an open plateau by the sea.

more.name: Rumassala
more.text: A fragment of the Sanjeevani mountain Hanuman carried. A coastal hill 20 min from Galle Fort.

cave.title: Ravana Cave, Ella: fit travellers only
cave.text: The cave tradition says Sita was hidden in is up 500–800 steep, often slippery steps, and it’s dark with bats inside. Your driver will wait while the younger ones climb; we don’t put it in the plan for elders.

factsNote: Timings and fees from public sources, October 2026. They change, so we check them again before your trip.
plansSub: One price for the whole car, split however many of you there are. Two or three places a day, temples in the morning puja window, a sit-down lunch and a rest in the afternoon.

About 3 h 20. Evening puja, night in Tissamaharama.
About 3½ h. Hanuman’s red earth, the Sanjeevani hill, sunset on the Fort walls.

months.title: Dry in the hills & south
months.text: Clear mornings at Seetha Eliya, calm sea at Galle. The easiest time for the whole trail.

months.title: Ram Navami
months.text: Expect crowds at the temples. Sinhala & Tamil New Year falls the same week, so book early.

months.title: Rain in the hills
months.text: Wetter in Nuwara Eliya, but Trincomalee and Koneswaram are at their best. Munneswaram’s festival runs Aug–Sep.

months.title: Showers everywhere
months.text: Afternoon rain across the island. Plan temples for the morning; Diwali falls in this window.

tips: Dress: shoulders and knees covered, shoes off at every temple. Some shrines have their own customs, so follow what others do or ask.
Food: tell us vegetarian, Jain or no onion-garlic and we’ll suggest lunch stops that fit.
Cold floors: Nuwara Eliya is at 1,868 m. Pack shawls and thick socks.
Hairpins: the Kandy–Nuwara Eliya road is winding. Carsick-prone? Your driver will stop whenever you need.
Buddhist sites: Divurumpola and Kelaniya are Buddhist temples. Dress modestly, take off shoes and hats, and ask at the temple how offerings are made.

items.a: Tradition places it at Seetha Eliya, where the Seetha Amman temple stands today; some say Hakgala gardens next door. They’re on the same road, so we take you to both.

items.q: How far is Ashok Vatika from Colombo and Kandy?
items.a: About 2 h 45 from Kandy by road, and about 5 h from Colombo or the airport. That’s why we break the journey in Kandy.

items.q: Can we travel from India by Ram Setu?
items.a: No. There’s no road or ferry across it. Fly to Colombo, or take the Nagapattinam–Kankesanthurai ferry to Jaffna. You can see where Ram Setu begins from Talaimannar, in Mannar.

items.q: Is it suitable for elderly parents?
items.a: Yes, that’s who the 6-day trip is built for. Most sites are flat or under 80 steps. We leave Ravana Cave and Sigiriya out for elders and keep every day short.

items.q: What are Seetha Amman temple timings?
items.a: 8 am–1 pm and 2–6:30 pm. Entry is free; a puja is about LKR 100–200.
